rationale: Start with a broad, mid-temperature scouting gradient to maximize the chance all 8 compounds elute and reveal the full retention window without excessive truncation risk. This run should show whether peaks are compressed early, late, or spread across the gradient so later injections can trim the window and adjust slope.

All peaks eluted within 4.07–9.38 min on the broad scout, corresponding roughly to phi_e about 0.20–0.44, so trim the gradient window around that region to spend gradient time where the peaks are and improve selectivity near the unresolved 4/5 pair. Keep tG and T unchanged so any resolution change is attributable mainly to the narrower phi window.

The narrow window improved the 4/5 pair but created a new 6/7 problem and pushed the last peak past 10 min, suggesting we should test pure slope sensitivity next. Doubling tG on the original broad window will show whether the critical close pairs separate with a shallower gradient without changing the phi range or temperature.

The close pairs are strongly slope-sensitive: at tG 40 all pairs are resolved, while tG 20 is too steep. Test the intermediate slope at the same broad window and temperature to find the shortest fully resolved condition, which should improve CRF by pulling t_last back toward 10 min.

Because one critical pair improves with shallower slope while another still behaves differently, temperature is the cleanest remaining lever to shift selectivity and potentially reorder or separate the unresolved neighbors without incurring the large time penalty of tG 40. Try a 15 C drop at the successful fast broad gradient to probe whether the bad pair is temperature-sensitive while keeping all peaks within 10 min or close to it.

Dropping temperature to 25 C nearly solved the selectivity problem, leaving only one marginal pair and a small time penalty. Test an intermediate temperature to see if that pair stays near or above 1.5 while pulling the last peak back closer to 10 min, which could beat the current best CRF.

At 25 C the separation is almost ideal and appears slope-sensitive enough that a slightly shallower gradient may push the remaining 1.38 pair over 1.5. Increasing tG by one step is the smallest change likely to gain full resolution, and the extra ~minute should still leave a strong CRF if all pairs resolve.

The 25 C, 20 min method is very close to optimal, and the peaks occupy only the central part of the broad gradient; narrowing the window slightly should flatten the effective slope in the critical region and may lift the marginal pair over 1.5. Using a modest trim rather than an aggressive one aims to preserve the good late-pair behavior and avoid the strong retention/time penalty seen before.

We now have full resolution with only a small time penalty, so the next move is to shorten the run until a pair approaches the 1.5 limit. Reducing tG by one step at the current successful window and temperature is the most direct test for a higher-CRF method.

Stay at the proven full-resolution conditions but raise phi0 one step to strengthen the gradient slightly and pull the chromatogram earlier, aiming to get t_last below 10 min. The first peak is still well retained, so this small trim should test whether we can cut the time penalty without sacrificing the critical 3/4 and 6/7 resolutions.

You already have the maximum CRF, so this is a risk-limited optimization probe: narrow and slightly steepen the successful window to see whether all pairs remain at or above 1.5 while keeping the last peak under 10 min. If it holds, it could match the optimum with a shorter practical run; if not, injection 10 remains the clear best.

Injection 11 still gives full resolution with the critical pair only just above threshold, so the logical next step is one more reduction in tG to find the shortest method that preserves R>=1.5 everywhere. This directly tests the boundary of failure while building on the best-performing phi window.

At tG 18 with phi0 0.15/phi1 0.85 the critical pair is only barely resolved, so a small increase in phi0 may shift the peaks earlier while preserving the effective selectivity of the proven narrow window. This probes whether we can keep full resolution and further shorten the practical run relative to injections 10–11.

The successful 0.15–0.85, 18 min method is right at the resolution threshold, so lowering phi1 one step should preserve a shallow effective slope while shifting the late peaks earlier and keeping the full-resolved pattern. This tests whether the upper end of the gradient window can be trimmed without losing the critical 3/4 separation.

Injection 14 has comfortable full resolution, especially for the former critical pair, so it is worth testing one faster step at the same phi window to see if all pairs still clear 1.5. If it succeeds, it gives a shorter fully resolved optimum; if not, injection 14 remains a robust best method.

The 0.15–0.80, 18 min method has strong resolution margin, so increasing phi0 one step may shift the chromatogram earlier while staying fully resolved. This is a focused test for an equally optimal but faster practical method near the current best region.

Injection 16 achieved full resolution with some margin and an earlier last peak than the other optimal methods, so one more 2-minute reduction in tG is the right boundary test. If all pairs remain at or above 1.5, this would identify the shortest fully resolved method in the current region.

The 0.20–0.80, 18 min method is fully resolved with moderate margin, so raising phi0 one step is a targeted attempt to move the chromatogram earlier while staying above the 1.5 threshold. This explores whether the lower edge of the window can be trimmed further without collapsing the persistent 3/4 pair.

Raising phi0 further hurt the critical 3/4 pair, so keep the proven lower edge at 0.20 and instead trim phi1 one step to test whether the upper end can be reduced while maintaining full resolution. This should preferentially move the later peaks earlier with less risk to the early critical pair than another phi0 increase.

Injection 19 has the strongest resolution margin among the 18 min optimal methods, so it is the best candidate for one more shortening step. Reducing tG to 16 min will test whether this tighter upper window can retain full resolution where other 16 min methods failed.

The 0.20–0.75, 18 min method has ample resolution margin, so a small temperature increase is a clean way to reduce actual analysis time while likely staying above the 1.5 threshold. This tests whether we can keep full resolution with a shorter practical run in the strongest current window.

Temperature increases are clearly unsafe, so return to 25 C and continue trimming only the upper edge of the strongest window. Lowering phi1 from 0.75 to 0.70 may preserve the now-comfortable critical separations while keeping the run fully resolved and potentially more focused.

With only a few injections left and several 1.000 methods already secured, use one exploratory point to see whether a slightly narrower and slightly longer window can keep full resolution while shifting the chromatogram into an even shorter practical pattern. The extra tG should protect the persistent 3/4 pair against the phi0 increase better than the failed 0.25–0.80, 18 min run.

Injection 23 gives full resolution with the last peak under 9 min, and its critical pair still has some margin, so reducing tG by one step is the best remaining boundary test. If resolution survives, this would define an even shorter fully resolved method than any current 1.000 condition.

For the last injection, test whether trimming phi1 one more step from the successful 0.25–0.75, 20 min method preserves the 3/4 pair while keeping the run fully resolved and centered earlier. This is the cleanest remaining unexplored neighbor of a proven 1.000 method.
